title: OneLake: The unified foundation for data, context, governance, and AI
author: diptiborkar

content.text:
If you haven’t already, read Arun Ulag’s Ignite blog post to learn how Microsoft is bringing together databases, analytics, and intelligent applications across Azure and Microsoft Fabric.
Most organizations' data is scattered across dozens of applications, clouds and services. Now that agents need to work across the entire business, organizations need to bring that data together in one place: one copy, open to every engine and team, without moving or duplicating it. Unified data gives agents reach, but to act with confidence they also need context: what the data means, how it connects to the business, who should see it and whether it can be trusted.
OneLake is the single place for customers to unify their data estate. Shortcuts, mirroring, catalog federation and IQ Share bring multi-cloud, on-premises sources and databases and data platforms together into a single view of the data estate. The OneLake catalog provides a trusted place for organizations to easily explore, govern and secure data in OneLake. It's integrated with every Fabric workload and one of the only lakes that governs data in both Delta Lake and Apache Iceberg open formats, making it truly open. Users can bring popular analytics and AI products and open-source projects to open data in OneLake.
Figure: OneLake provides an open, governed foundation for Fabric workloads.
OneLake handles over 110 billion interactions a day, and data stored natively in OneLake is backed by 4 million storage accounts. In addition, more than 240,000 organizations use the OneLake catalog to govern more than 350 million data items. The catalog is embedded in more than 100 apps people use every day, including Foundry, Power BI, Teams, and Excel.
At Microsoft Ignite, we're taking the next step and making OneLake catalog the center of Microsoft's data governance strategy, delivering new capabilities that bring data, context, and governance together for AI, and expanding the partner ecosystem that extends OneLake across the wider data estate. Here's what that means to you.
The OneLake Catalog: Governance where your data lives
Customers have told us consistently that running a standalone catalog alongside their data platform creates friction, and that they want governance to live where data is analyzed and put to work. The market has moved the same way, with leading data platforms building governance directly into the analytics experience. Fabric has always had a lake-first data foundation with OneLake, and OneLake catalog already has market leading governance and administration.
Figure: OneLake catalog brings data discovery, governance and security together on OneLake, with Copilot built in.
This is where Microsoft has strong momentum.
We’re making a definitive announcement: OneLake catalog is now Microsoft’s data governance product. This isn't something new either. The OneLake catalog has been the trusted catalog for Fabric data for years, and we're now deepening our investment in it. From a single place, teams can deliver on three main tasks:
• Explore: Easily discover and understand data across the estate, with lineage, permissions and business context on every item.
• Govern: See governance insights and recommended actions, and manage domains, tags, endorsements and policies centrally.
• Secure: Manage OneLake security roles and fine-grained permissions in one central hub.
As part of this data governance evolution, Microsoft Purview Data Governance will be retired, and new data governance innovation will land in the OneLake catalog. We want to be clear about what this means. The OneLake catalog takes a different approach: rather than cataloging metadata wherever it lives, it governs the data that lives in or is connected to OneLake through native items, federated catalogs, IQ Shares, Shortcuts and Mirrored databases. That makes it a new model, not a feature-for-feature replacement for Purview Data Governance. Purview Data Security and Compliance, including Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention, Insider Risk Management and Data Security Posture Management, are not affected and continue to protect your data in Fabric.
OneLake catalog brings discovery, governance, and security together where data is managed and used. Generally available capabilities help teams find and understand trusted data, monitor governance health, and enforce consistent protections. Govern Skills help identify gaps and prioritize action.
We have enhanced further with richer discovery across granular data objects, improved search and lineage, and new Curation and Protection Skills. These skills extend AI-assisted governance beyond health assessments, helping organizations improve metadata quality, identify protection gaps, and take action with AI assistance. Together, these capabilities make it easier to find trusted data, understand how it's being used, and manage governance and security at scale. With Data governance being a core priority for us and our customers – we will continue expanding these capabilities with Data Quality, enhanced curation with glossaries, enhanced granular lineage, additional policies for guardrails, and more. All with the goal to allow governing your data at scale and ensuring your data is ready for AI.
Strategic partnership with Atlan to extend data governance
Today we are announcing a strategic partnership with Atlan aligned with our lake-first data governance approach. OneLake and Fabric customers can use Atlan, Microsoft’s preferred data governance partner, to extend governance beyond OneLake. The OneLake catalog provides native governance across Fabric and connected data, while Atlan complements it across the broader data estate. Atlan also provides granular, cross-estate lineage and richer governance constructs such as usage and popularity stats across heterogeneous, non-Microsoft data sources, and supports customers transitioning from Purview Data Governance to Fabric with tooling to carry their existing metadata forward.
Figure: OneLake and Atlan provide complementary governance across the broader data estate.
Governance gives organizations confidence in their data. The next step is making that data, and the context around it, ready for AI.
New in OneLake: Bringing data and context together for AI
Governance is the foundation, but AI needs more than well-governed tables. Agents need the context and permissions that travel with the data. Today we're introducing new OneLake capabilities that close that gap:
IQ sharing in OneLake and Fabric (Preview)
At FabCon Barcelona, we introduced IQ sharing, which lets organizations share data and context with other Fabric tenants without copying data. Partners such as S&P Global, TomTom, EY, xMentium, Sitecore, Xoople, and Financial Fabric use it to prepare their data and expertise once and deliver it to many customers in Fabric by listing their integrations in OneLake catalog. Now IQ Sharing adds Fabric IQ Ontologies as an Item that customers can share, so providers can share the business entities, relationships and definitions that describe their data along with the data itself.
Figure: Animated GIF - Sharing data with other Fabric tenants through IQ sharing.
AI Search (Microsoft Foundry) support for OneLake with OneLake security (Preview)
Agents built in Microsoft Foundry can use data stored in OneLake. The OneLake catalog is available in Foundry, and OneLake items, including shortcuts and mirrored items, can be added as knowledge sources in Foundry IQ (Preview). With OneLake catalog embedded in Microsoft Foundry, developers can explore enterprise data with rich metadata, endorsements, and sensitivity labels, then easily connect trusted data to their AI agents while respecting existing permissions and governance.
Figure: OneLake data is indexed for use in Microsoft Foundry.
Read and write with credential vending in OneLake Table APIs (Generally Available)
Fabric customers using Iceberg-compatible engines such as ClickHouse, Snowflake and Teradata can now read and write Iceberg tables through OneLake Table APIs with credential vending. This lets teams work from a single copy of their data in OneLake using the engines they already rely on, while keeping access secure and removing the overhead of managing storage permissions.
• Read and write using Iceberg REST: Engines can read and write Iceberg tables in OneLake using the Iceberg REST APIs.
• Simpler access management: Credential vending delegates access control to the catalog, so users no longer need to manage storage permissions manually.
• Fine-grained security: Row- and column-level permissions defined with OneLake security on Iceberg tables further control access when the data is used in Fabric.
Semantic views (Preview)
Fabric customers can now define business metrics once, alongside their data in OneLake, and reuse them across AI and BI experiences. Semantic views capture tables, relationships, and metrics in an open YAML format based on Apache Ossie (incubating), separately from the engines and tools that consume them. Combined with OneLake shortcuts, teams can reuse centrally maintained definitions across lakehouses without copying them. The result is a consistent, governed foundation that keeps every user grounded in the same trusted business context.
Figure: Semantic views define reusable business metrics and context in Fabric.
These innovations build on strong momentum: OneLake handles more than 110 billion interactions a day across more than 15 million active shortcuts, and storage has grown more than 300% year over year. And because every one of these capabilities is built on open standards, they're just as valuable to the partners building on OneLake as they are to our customers.
An open ecosystem built on OneLake
OneLake is open and interoperable, enabling a growing ecosystem to build on it. Nearly 50 ISV and open-source partners now work with OneLake's open Table APIs across data access, sharing, movement and operations. That lets customers keep the tools they rely on while making OneLake the center of their data estate.
Figure: OneLake partners support data access, sharing, movement, and operations.
At Ignite, we're expanding the ecosystem with new capabilities and partnerships:
Catalog federation (Generally Available)
Tables from Dremio catalog, Azure Monitor logs, AWS Glue catalog, Google Lakehouse runtime catalog, and CONNECT by AVEVA now appear in OneLake with zero data movement or duplication. Built on industry-standard Apache Iceberg REST catalog (IRC) APIs, catalog federation stays in sync with each source catalog and automatically creates OneLake shortcuts, so federated tables are accessible in Fabric and ready for Copilot, Spark, Power BI and Fabric data agents.
Azure Databricks native storage (Generally Available)
Fabric customers using Azure Databricks can store their data natively in OneLake, so they can work from a single copy of their data, use a shared governance model, and choose the analytics and AI tools that best fit their needs.
IQ Sharing launch partners
Data providers such as S&P Global, TomTom, EY, Financial Fabric, xMentium, LSEG, Dun & Bradstreet, Sitecore, and Xoople can use IQ Sharing to share data and context securely across tenants without copying the data. Customers can easily discover new and shared data in the OneLake catalog, which is available in Microsoft Fabric, Foundry, Copilot Studio, and Power BI.
Figure: IQ Sharing launch partners extend data and context across organizations.
IQ Sharing Launch Partner Capabilities
Financial Fabric’s Capital Markets DataHub on Microsoft Fabric IQ Share enables institutional investors to discover, configure, and consume trusted, governed, AI-ready financial data and analytics directly within their Microsoft Fabric environments—in minutes, without client-side ETL. Backed by Financial Fabric's fully managed data service, DataHub provides access to over 200 capital markets data providers and more than 10,000 datasets.
Xoople’s foundational Earth data helps customers understand where conditions may be changing across large corridor networks, so its specialists can focus drones, LiDAR, field inspection, and engineering resources where closer investigation is warranted. With IQ Sharing, Xoople delivers governed earth data directly in the customer’s OneLake enabling them to focus their investigation and resources where it is needed more. To learn more, watch the Microsoft Fabric + Xoople + Verdantasnd video.
Figure: Xoople shares governed Earth data through IQ Sharing.
xMentium transforms more than 100,000 complex, unstructured enterprise documents daily into structured, AI-ready data, unlocking valuable insights from engineering drawings, contracts, and technical records. Through IQ sharing in Microsoft Fabric, xMentium enables organizations to seamlessly discover and leverage this intelligence in OneLake, accelerating analytics and AI-driven innovation. To learn more, watch the xMentium: Microsoft IQ Sharing Launch Partner video.
Figure: xMentium shares ontology-based business context through IQ Sharing.
Salesforce Data 360 shortcut (Preview)
Fabric and Salesforce customers can now bring Salesforce customer data into OneLake with zero ETL, so it can be unified with the rest of the enterprise data estate for relevant and accurate analytics and AI.
Figure: A Salesforce Data 360 shortcut makes Salesforce data available in OneLake.
Each of these partnerships connects more of the data estate into OneLake and extends what customers can do with it, so organizations spend less time stitching platforms together and more time putting their data to work.
Looking ahead
With OneLake, customers have one foundation for their data, OneLake catalog to govern it and an open ecosystem to extend it, for analytics and for AI. That's the thread running through everything we're announcing at Ignite. We'll keep investing in OneLake, deepening our work with partners and removing barriers between platforms, so you have the flexibility to build your data and AI projects your way. We believe connecting the world's data empowers customers to do more with it, and in the AI era, Fabric makes that easier than ever. We look forward to helping you get there.
To learn more, check out the following resources:
• OneLake documentation
• OneLake catalog documentation
• Join us at Ignite for BRK351, Unify your data estate with Microsoft OneLake.
